body: All cookies handled by the cookie component are expected to be encrypted by default. You can disable encryption using the config() method.

I really need the encryption to work with some cookies, like remember me feature in the login, disable the encryption is not the best option, but I need other cookies only to share with jquery, only that I need is fix the error message, in order to do this, I dont need read or write these cookies using cookie component. I use a php statement to do this, but the cookie component always try to decrypt an non encrypted cookie. 
Now it is impossible to use cookies with Cookie component and other cookies in javascript or another way, as I was saying the component does not need to read those other cookies, but should not have conflict with them. The developer should know that if he wrote the cookie using the component this is encrypted and only can read using the component and vice versa
You can read cookies written through query by simply using `$_COOKIE['test']` :stuck_out_tongue:

Then you can encrypt some cookies but not others using the `configKey()` method. The [documentation has an example of this](http://book.cakephp.org/3.0/en/core-libraries/components/cookie.html#configuring-cookies).

Let me know if this works, of if there is an alternative API that would work better.

Ok, have you tried doing `$this->Cookie->configKey('test', 'encryption', false);` in the beforeFilter() before reading the cookie value? That will make cookie component expect the `test` cookie to be un-encrypted.
I think it makes sense not to throw errors when unencrypted cookies are set

I also thought about that solution , but as you say disable encryption by default is not the best solution, as it says @lorenzo , not throw errors when unencrypted cookies are set is the best solution for these cases.

In these cases the developer should know if try to read those unencrypted  cookies using the component without specifying that does not have encryption it may fail

I think exceptions **should** be thrown when an application is expecting encrypted data and does not get it. To me not throwing an exception voids the entire point of encrypted cookies. For example:
- I have a cookie with sensitive data, that the client should not tamper with, so I encrypt it.
- If an attacker can figure out the general structure of the data, they can simply replace the encrypted cookie with a plaintext one and easily defeat any and all protections my application may get from encrypting the cookie.

I agree exceptions should be thrown when encryption is expected. But there are plenty sources a cookie can come from, for example those set from javascript. Maybe having a list of the cookies you expect to read would help?
What if cookie data is lazily read as keys are accessed? That would fix the issues around decrypting all the cookies.
Ok, I can work on making that happen. In hindsight eagerly reading and decrypting all the cookies on every request is pretty wasteful.

issue.body:
Individual cookie values are now read on an ad hoc basis as they are accessed. This alleviates issues where javascript libraries add cookies that CookieComponent does not know about. Previously, these cookies would trigger encrypted cookie warnings.

Unfortunately reading cookies lazily means we don't have a way to read _all_ cookies.

Refs #3814

body: Closing again as #3827 introduces lazy cookie decryption which solves the issues described here around eagerly decrypting cookie data.
